Just to clarify, the current AI Quality Workforce Intelligence demo and my T3 Code integration experiment are two separate things. 😄

I'm keeping the existing demo focused on QA workforce management, skill-based allocation, and release readiness. The T3 Code work is a separate experiment where I'm exploring how AI coding workflows could be independently tested and verified. I'm not mixing that into the current demo.

Regarding the dashboard, the strongest feedback so far has been around release readiness, especially how a high pass rate can be misleading when only a small percentage of tests have actually been executed.

Skill-based allocation also received positive feedback, particularly the visibility into missing skills.

I'm now planning to speak with QA leaders to understand which metrics they genuinely rely on when deciding whether a release is ready.

The goal is to improve the existing product based on real user feedback while exploring T3 Code separately. If the experiment proves useful, I'll evaluate how it could add value later.
